title: Refactor `config::get` to split off two helper functions
description:
This PR splits off two new internal helper functions from `config::get`:

- `load_config` as a wrapper for `yaml::yaml.load_file` and
- `eval_config` for recursive evaluation.

Splitting this functionality out of `config::get` allows users to avoid the requirement that the config file include a "default" key (per #13) since `load_config(file) |> eval_config()` covers a good part of the functionality of `config::get()`.

title: eval expressions in parent environment
description:
Hi config maintainers.

Before #29, I think R expressions were evaluated in the environment that called `config::get` rather than the `base_env`. I was using this functionality to base config variables off of 
1. command line arguments
2. create somewhat verbose new arguments based off of previously loaded config files (`!expr server` vs `!expr config::get("server", file = "/etc/server-config.yml")`

Some of my current config workflows were broken after #29, I think this also related to this [comment](https://github.com/rstudio/config/issues/20#issuecomment-762733391) on #20.

Was changing to evaluating expressions in the `base_env()` an intended change? Please let me know if I should make any changes to this PR. Thanks for your work on this helpful package!

title: Eval only after the configuration was merged.  Possible fix for #20
description:
At the moment, all `!expr` statements in the config file are evaluated, even if these are not relevant for the active configuration.   This PR proposes a fix to read the yaml file with `eval.expr = FALSE` (using a handler) and then evaluates these statements only after the merge is completed.  I also add additional test cases (that fail with current code base, but passes with the proposed fix).

This is hopefully a fix for #20

title: allow multiple active configurations
description:
This PR implements support for multiple named configurations being active at the same time. The thinking is that some environments (e.g. shinyapps) might want to automatically define an active configuration while at the same time enabling customers to specify additional named configurations. Configuration names might also be used as "facets", e.g.

``` yaml
default:
    server: localhost:5555

production:
    server: server.example.com

east:
    server: server-east.example.com
```

All production configurations would use "server.example.com" by default however when the configuration is `c("production", "east")` then "server-east.example.com" is used.

It could be argued that this is just sugar over inheritance (maybe that's true or maybe there are some subtle differences).  Even if that's true I think there is benefit for environments (e.g. shinyapps) to be able to automatically define active configuration names w/o forcing users to grapple with them (i.e. they are there if you want to take advantage of them but can be ignored if you don't). For example, consider this config file:

``` yaml
default:
    sample: 1000
    server: localhost:5555

production:
    sample: null
    server: server.example.com
```

If the user configures a deployed app to have the "production" configuration name on shinyapps then this will work as expected out of the box (even if shinyapps also adds itself as a named configuration). If the user subsequently wants to use a special `server` value for shinyapps, they need only do:

``` yaml
default:
    sample: 1000
    server: localhost:5555

production:
    sample: null
    server: server.example.com

shinyapps:
    server: ec2-server.aws.com
```

Compare this to:

``` yaml
shinyapps: 
   inherits: production
   server: ec2-server.aws.com
```

All of that said, I don't have super strong feelings about this and if others think that multiple active configurations is problematic and we should rely on inheritance then I'm fine with that. One significant argument in favor of inheritance is that the priority of merging configurations is more explicit (in the case of multiple active configurations _later_ configurations in the list have priority since they syntactically qualify configurations to their left but this might not be obvious).

@tareefk @jcheng5 @hadley

@aronatkins This is a new **config** package used for reading values from configuration profiles for different environments, see the [README](https://github.com/rstudio/config/blob/feature/active-configurations/README.md) for additional context.
